'''''Epilobium tetragonum''''', commonly known as the '''square stalked willow herb''', is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the willowherb family [[Onagraceae]].

The erect perennial herb typically grows to a height of {{convert|0.1|to|1.3|m|ft|1}} and can have several stems. It blooms between January and November{{clarify|reason=where?|date=July 2020}} and produces pink-purple flowers.

The species has become naturalised in the [[Perth, Western Australia|Perth]] and [[Peel (Western Australia)|Peel]] regions of Western Australia.<ref>{{Florabase|title=Epilobium tetragonum|id=1753}}</ref>

==Description==
<gallery>
File:Epilobium tetragonum-SeattleWA.jpeg|Overhead view of small ''E. tetragonum'' plant

''Epilobium tetragonum'' is characterized by its distinctive square-shaped stem, with leaves evenly spaced in a tetragonal arrangement around the stem, giving the plant a square-like appearance. The leaves are hairless and solid green and have a unique shimmer in direct sunlight.<ref>{{cite web |title=WIllow herb |url=http://www.herbiguide.com.au/Descriptions/hg_Willow_Herb.htm |website=herbiguide.com |access-date=16 April 2023}}</ref>
